                   OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES

1.   Scheme

     The Government of India has introduced an old age pension scheme for all land
holding Small and Marginal Farmers (SMFs)  in the country, namely, the “Pradhan
Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY)”, as a voluntary and contributory
pension scheme for the entry age group of 18 to 40 years. The Scheme is effective from
the 9th August, 2019.

2.    Objective and Benefits

      There have been a series of interventions for income and price support by the
Government for farmers. However, there is a felt need to create a social security net for
the farmers as old age may result in loss of livelihood for many of them.  Farming
requires hard work in fields which becomes difficult at an advanced age. The problem is
compounded in respect of small and marginal farmers as they have minimal or no savings
to provide for old age. The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) provides
for an assured monthly pension of Rs. 3000/- to  all land holding Small and Marginal
Farmers (SMFs), whether male or female, on their attaining the age of 60 years. Farmers
falling within the purview  of the exclusion  criteria (as defined  in Para 5  of these
guidelines)  are, however, not  eligible  for the  benefit. The key features and other
consequential benefits accruing to the subscribers of the Scheme are detailed further in
these guidelines.
